title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses Delhi Police of Silencing Women Over Harassment Complaints
excerpt: The Leader of Opposition said women protesters and journalists faced mistreatment by Delhi Police during October 3 demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, and demanded CCTV footage from Saket police station be made public.
body:
• Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday accused Delhi Police of mistreating women protesters and journalists during the October 3 demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, describing "a single pattern: silence any woman who dares to ask questions."
  • Three women journalists alleged manhandling and sexual harassment by police personnel during their detention at the protest against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Delhi Police confirmed receiving the complaints, conducted medical examinations, and referred the matter to the Crime Branch.
  • Gandhi also cited two women, Shaheen and Nafisa, who alleged violence inside Saket police station weeks ago, and demanded the station's full CCTV footage be made public along with action against guilty officers.
  • The episode widens the political confrontation over the SIR exercise and the demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The Press Council of India expressed "shock and dismay" over the treatment of journalists covering the protests.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday accused the Delhi Police of mistreating women protesters and journalists during recent demonstrations in the national capital, after three women who identified themselves as journalists complained of manhandling and sexual harassment by police personnel during their detention at an October 3 protest.

Gandhi posted on X alongside a video of his recent interaction with two journalists, Shaheen Khan and Nafisa Khan, who he said were assaulted at Saket police station weeks ago after covering an event attended by Home Minister Amit Shah.

"What's happening in Delhi right now follows a single pattern: silence any woman who dares to ask questions. Hundreds of people were detained at Jantar Mantar. Female protesters alleged that male police officers misbehaved with them. Cameras were snatched from female journalists, and they were dragged around. Not even an FIR was filed on a journalist's complaint."

— Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha

Context & Background

The October 3 protest near Jantar Mantar, organised by the All India Students' Association and other groups, opposed the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police said Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita had been imposed in the area; protesters who refused to vacate were detained, and at least three FIRs were registered in connection with protests on October 2 and 3.

https://x.com/aprajitanefes/status/2106666007897260071

The SIR controversy intensified after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months concerning electoral rolls — claims the Election Commission rejected as routine administrative inputs. Successive demonstrations at Jantar Mantar have drawn hundreds of detentions.

Gandhi linked the October 3 allegations to the earlier Saket episode and to the force's chain of command: "And everyone in this country knows who the Delhi Police answers to" — a reference to the Union Home Ministry, which controls the capital's police. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra separately questioned the prime minister and Shah, saying "the very police whose job it is to provide security is making women feel threatened."

Impact & Analysis

Delhi Police has acknowledged the complaints. Deputy Commissioner of Police Neha Yadav said the three women lodged their complaint at around 6 pm on October 3, medical examinations were conducted, and the matter was referred to the Crime Branch. The force confirmed on X that it had received allegations of sexual harassment by police personnel and asked anyone with relevant footage to share it with investigators.

The unresolved question of an FIR is the immediate flashpoint. AAP's Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj staged a demonstration outside Parliament Street police station demanding one. With no official explanation offered for the timeline, critics have treated the delay as reluctance to pursue a case that could embarrass the administration. The Press Council of India expressed "shock and dismay" over the treatment of journalists covering the demonstration and called on Delhi Police to act on the complaints.

Diaspora Angle

For overseas Indians, who follow Indian political developments closely, the standoff adds another flashpoint to the SIR controversy and the broader debate over policing of protests and press freedom in the world's largest democracy. Diaspora media and community forums have tracked the electoral-roll dispute for weeks; allegations of misconduct against women journalists give it a sharper edge.

What's Next

The Crime Branch inquiry is the near-term test — whether an FIR is registered, against whom, and on what timeline. Gandhi's demand for the release of Saket police station's CCTV footage is the other pressure point. Beyond that, the SIR protests show no sign of abating, and how the Election Commission and the Centre respond will determine whether this remains a policing controversy or escalates further.
